planningNote: The launch queue covers eight US attractions, including the existing Golden Gate Bridge page, and retains the San Francisco trip-planning briefs. Publish eligible prepared articles within the Asia/Shanghai daily limit. Search Console observations guide ranking when available; the launch shortlist is an editorial selection.

topics.primaryIntent: What should I check before using transit from SFO with luggage?
topics.brief: A practical pre-departure and arrival decision checklist for airport transit with luggage. Explain how to compare hotel access, transfers, walking and fallback choices without inventing prices, timetables or safety guarantees.
topics.reviewNote: Potential intent overlap with an existing review guide; confirm an independent reader task before making ready. Consolidate useful checklist items into the existing SFO transfer guide unless query evidence establishes another task.

topics.primaryIntent: How can I plan a flexible waterfront sightseeing day using public transit?
topics.brief: A flexible sightseeing decision guide combining waterfront visits and a historic streetcar. Include mobility considerations, a walking fallback and a short versus long visit choice without invented schedules.

topics.primaryIntent: What should I check before visiting the Golden Gate Bridge by transit?
topics.brief: A before-you-leave checklist covering which bridge end, pedestrian access verification, weather and return transit research. Provide decision support; do not give unverified service hours or promise current route numbers.
topics.reviewNote: Potential intent overlap with an existing review guide; confirm an independent reader task before making ready. Consolidate verified pre-departure checks into the existing bridge guide unless new reader evidence establishes another task.

topics.primaryIntent: How should several adults assign contactless cards or devices before entering transit gates?
topics.brief: Solve the group coordination task for adult riders: create a rider-to-credential worksheet and agree on a meeting point after the gates without assuming staff can override payment rules. Use the registered Clipper separate-riders fact and BART airport-station fact. Apply same-credential entry/exit matching only where that operator requires both taps; never infer that every service has an exit tap or give unregistered Muni tap instructions. Distinguish adults using their own credentials from youth/discount eligibility; refer those readers to official programs without inventing conditions. Do not assert that multiple devices on one bank account always work, quote prices, promise acceptance of a particular foreign bank card, or invent a fix for declined payment. Include a practical pre-boarding checklist and a decision table explaining when to pause and consult the operator.
topics.reviewNote: The revised BART/Muni guide already has a per-rider payment section covering separate credentials, matching entry/exit where required, eligibility and backup preparation. A worksheet or meeting-point checklist alone does not justify a separate full guide. Prefer improving the existing guide unless verified new group-specific rules or real reader questions establish an independent task.
topics.distinctness: Potential worksheet extension to the existing operator/payment guide; independent article value has not been established.

topics.primaryIntent: How can I verify a step-free F-line waterfront journey stop by stop?
topics.brief: Build a stop-level accessibility verification worksheet covering boarding platform, vehicle boarding arrangement, destination access and the return stop. Keep wheelchair/stroller questions separate from a general sightseeing itinerary. Link official access information and explain what remains unconfirmed. Do not guarantee step-free access, assume all historic streetcars or stops are interchangeable, invent ramp locations, or reuse the luggage-transfer article as a substitute.
topics.distinctness: A stop-by-stop access decision task; the general waterfront itinerary remains a separate sightseeing task.
topics.reviewNote: Official access procedures, selected-stop distinctions and current-notice/temporary-stop lookup entry points were semantically reviewed on 2026-10-21. Existing access-source hash still matches; new lookup hashes are proposed for manual PR adoption. Ready means eligible for a checked draft after that PR, not verified equipment availability or permission to promise a step-free trip. Ask the operator if the named stop or fallback cannot be confirmed.

topics.primaryIntent: How can I tell whether the ride I want is a cable car or an F-line historic streetcar?
topics.brief: Help a visitor identify the intended transit experience before choosing a route: compare the two modes using verified operator descriptions, map lookup steps and clearly licensed reference photographs. Include a mode-identification checklist and explain where to verify route and boarding information. Avoid copying the pass break-even article, calling every historic vehicle a cable car, promising a specific vehicle on a departure, or publishing unregistered fares and operating hours. Use the existing licensed F-line photograph and official mode/route links as references; do not invent or hotlink a cable-car photograph. Keep fares and pass arithmetic in the existing pass guide.
topics.distinctness: Identify the ride and mode a visitor actually wants; ticket-price comparison stays with the existing pass guide.
topics.reviewNote: SFMTA mode names, the cable mechanism, route-identification/boarding signs and the accessible-boarding limitation were reviewed on 2026-10-21; its new baseline is a manual PR adoption proposal. No specific departure, vehicle allocation, queue or fare amount was verified.

topics.primaryIntent: How should a family check child and youth fare eligibility separately for BART and Muni?
topics.brief: Provide a family planning worksheet that records each rider's age category, operator, required payment credential and evidence to confirm eligibility. Compare verification steps rather than inventing a universal family ticket. Explicitly separate adult contactless payment from discount programs. Do not infer child eligibility from adult fare records, promise free travel, or invent an age threshold or application requirement.
topics.distinctness: Family eligibility and credential preparation, not an adult pass comparison or a repeat of the operator overview.
topics.reviewNote: SFMTA youth conditions and its machine baseline were verified on 2026-10-21. Keep regular Muni universal youth travel separate from cable-car/residency exceptions; ID for 16+ is encouraged, not mandatory. BART requires a qualifying Youth Clipper credential for the listed discount; do not promise airport issuance, overseas delivery or an adult bank-tap discount. The missing machine baselines were captured by real GitHub runner run 39603328748 and reviewed in PR #21; the local 403 limitation no longer leaves these source hashes missing.

topics.primaryIntent: What should I verify if my SFO arrival is too late for my planned BART connection?
topics.brief: Build an after-a-delay decision flow based on actual arrival readiness, official journey planners and verified airport ground-transport options. Explain how to abandon a missed connection and select a qualified alternative without declaring a timetable guarantee. Include a worksheet for the correct travel date and destination. Do not copy the normal airport-to-Wharf luggage route, invent last-train times, promise overnight service, or give unverified pickup locations and prices.
topics.distinctness: Recover from a disrupted late arrival; the existing airport guide covers a planned routine transfer.
topics.reviewNote: Official SFO pickup pages and candidate machine hashes were verified on 2026-10-21. Use the actual travel date, readiness time and destination in BART tools; no specific last departure or interchange was queried. Do not add an unverified overnight bus or guarantee taxi/ride-app supply, cost, child seats or wait time. The missing machine baselines were captured by real GitHub runner run 39603328748 and reviewed in PR #21; the local 403 limitation no longer leaves these source hashes missing.

topics.primaryIntent: What official checks should I make when my transit contactless payment is declined?
topics.brief: Create a bounded troubleshooting decision table using operator and payment-program guidance: distinguish a credential mismatch, an operator instruction and a bank-related issue only where official documentation supports that distinction. Explain when to stop retrying and contact the responsible provider. Do not diagnose an account as blocked from a single failed tap, promise a reversal/refund, invent bank-card compatibility rules, or recommend bypassing gates.
topics.distinctness: Recover from a failed payment, rather than explain operator coverage or ordinary tap preparation.
topics.reviewNote: Separate a failed tap from the specific documented issuer-rejected pre-authorization condition; do not diagnose bank blocking from one red light or apply Auto-Reload BAD DEBT instructions to bank contactless. Staff/Clipper support and pre-journey Clipper alternatives are documented; no general promise of bank resolution, refunds or a recovery time was verified. An existing paid-area journey must be resolved with staff before changing credentials. The missing machine baselines were captured by real GitHub runner run 39603328748 and reviewed in PR #21; the local 403 limitation no longer leaves these source hashes missing.

topics.primaryIntent: How should I compare the ferry and bus return before a car-free Sausalito day trip?
topics.brief: Start with the return journey and compare which terminal/stop, operator, travel date and ticket conditions a visitor must check. Give a decision worksheet for a shorter or longer visit and a fallback if the chosen return no longer works. Do not promise boarding capacity, invent a combined ticket, copy the Golden Gate Bridge walk guide, or quote unverified schedules, fares or reservation rules. Use the registered direction-specific bus and ferry lookup facts only while their short manual validity remains current. Do not copy the temporary October timetable or promise a date-specific final return; the official travel-date and alert check is a required reader step.
topics.distinctness: A town day-trip return-mode decision, separate from bridge access and walking.
topics.reviewNote: Rendered official bus direction/stop and ferry terminal/day-type lookup were manually checked on 2026-10-21. Two dynamic facts deliberately omit machine evidence and expire at 2026-10-24 00:00 UTC; normal monitoring cannot renew them. Draft the comparison worksheet only while these records are current, and manually recheck before a later release. Temporary ferry notices override the regular table; no last departure, capacity, boarding gate or accessible walking path is certified. See docs/sausalito-source-review-2026-10-21.md.

topics.primaryIntent: How should I use official BART and Muni alerts to revise a disrupted sightseeing journey?
topics.brief: Develop an alert-to-action worksheet: identify the affected operator and segment, distinguish a station/stop issue from a whole-route disruption when official guidance allows it, re-plan the journey and recheck the return. Verify the advisory's issue/update date and applicable time range; an official page can still link to an expired incident. Link the live advisory index and represent any necessary precise date in expiring fact records instead of copying temporary incidents into evergreen prose. Do not invent a detour, promise replacement transport or accessibility, or present a historical advisory as current.
topics.distinctness: A current service-disruption response workflow, not another general route overview or payment guide.
topics.reviewNote: Current SFMTA advisory/relocation/planner entry points and example notices were reviewed on 2026-10-21. Read each notice's update date, affected segment, direction and effective period: official indexes can retain old incidents. No current incident, accessible detour or replacement bus is certified by a stable page hash; a specific substitute must be checked with its operator. The SFMTA elevator page concerns Muni Metro, not every F-line wayside lift. The missing machine baselines were captured by real GitHub runner run 39603328748 and reviewed in PR #21; the local 403 limitation no longer leaves these source hashes missing.

topics.primaryIntent: What should I see on a first visit to the Grand Canyon South Rim?
topics.brief: Help a first-time visitor choose a South Rim viewpoint and an optional rim walk. Use Mather Point, the changing perspective along the Canyon Rim Trail, and what the canyon walls reveal. Guide readers to official access and trail updates before travel.

topics.primaryIntent: What should I see on a first Yellowstone geyser-basin visit?
topics.brief: Make a thermal-focused first visit easy to picture. Anchor on Old Faithful and the Upper Geyser Basin boardwalks. Explain Grand Prismatic as a separate Midway Geyser Basin stop, and emphasize current conditions and official safety rules.

topics.primaryIntent: Which Yosemite Valley viewpoints should I choose for a first visit?
topics.brief: Pair Tunnel View with one valley-floor stop. Describe what the visitor can look for from each, the seasonal variability of the falls, and the official checks for road access, trail conditions, and entry arrangements.

topics.primaryIntent: How should I choose between a Liberty Island visit, the pedestal and the crown?
topics.brief: Frame the official island visit as a waterfront attraction. Compare grounds and museum, pedestal and crown choices without assuming ticket inclusions or elevator access. Include departure-side, screening and Ellis Island planning.

topics.primaryIntent: Which monuments should I pair on a first National Mall visit?
topics.brief: Build an outdoor memorial-focused first visit around the Washington Monument and Lincoln Memorial, with the Reflecting Pool as a visual connection and optional nearby memorials. Link to official route and access notices.

topics.primaryIntent: What should I prioritize at Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex?
topics.brief: Anchor the visit on the actual Space Shuttle Atlantis display. Compare a main-campus exhibition focus with adding the bus tour to Apollo/Saturn V, and point to current operating and event guidance without promising launch or tour access.

topics.primaryIntent: What should I see on a first visit to Balboa Park in San Diego?
topics.brief: Anchor a first visit on El Prado, the Botanical Building and the Lily Pond. Match an optional museum or garden to interests and explain which checks apply to individual venue hours, arrival and parking.

topics.primaryIntent: What should I see at the Golden Gate Bridge on a first visit?
topics.brief: Surface the existing Golden Gate Bridge page through the US attractions list. Its separate attraction overview covers the view and engineering exhibits, with the original transport guidance beneath it.

topics.primaryIntent: How can I plan a first visit to Acadia's rocky coast from Sand Beach along Ocean Path?
topics.brief: Give first-time visitors a flexible coastal outing on Mount Desert Island with Sand Beach, Thunder Hole, and an optional extension toward Otter Cliffs. Explain the contrast between the beach cove and exposed granite shore, point out when to turn back, and direct readers to official alerts, access and safety information.

topics.primaryIntent: Can I combine Bathhouse Row and the Grand Promenade on a first visit to Hot Springs National Park?
topics.brief: Help a first-time visitor combine the historic bathhouses on Central Avenue with a short Grand Promenade outing. Treat the Fordyce museum as conditional on access, explain street-to-hillside approaches, and distinguish seeing thermal springs from arranging an operated bath.
